request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has an **Export (CSV)** button (`person-export`) that downloads a file starting with `cell,value`, then one line for each of the ten cells in the order you gave. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The change is one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/export/personExport.slot.tsx`, which adds the button and an "Export" column heading. No server or stored-data change was needed.

**How it gets the values:** the button copies each cell's text straight from that person's row on screen, so every value matches what the row shows. Values containing a comma are quoted (e.g. `"Lee, Jo (B)"`), using the CSV helper the other exports already use.

**Hidden columns:** if a user has switched one of these columns off, it isn't on screen, so its line in the file has an empty value. I took "as the row shows it" literally. If you'd rather the file always carry the real figure, the export would need to work the values out itself, as the sheet-wide exports do, instead of copying them from the screen. The tests don't hide any columns, so they don't cover this case.
